title: Type the address yourself
takeaway: Open mint sites only from links you have checked on two official channels, then bookmark them.

cards.title: One letter off
cards.body: Presale is close. You search for the mint site and tap the first result. It has the dragons, the colors and a countdown. In this practice, the real site is pocketdragons.example. The address looks right at a glance. Look again, letter by letter.

url.label: Secure prefix
url.why: https only means encrypted, not honest.

url.label: Lookalike domain
url.why: An m where the n should be.

page.title: Pocket Dragons presale
lines: Presale is live. Connect to join.

cards.title: How fakes look real
cards.body: Fake sites copy the art, the words and the countdown. The one thing they cannot copy is the exact domain. Watch for a swapped letter, an extra word like claim or mint, or a different ending. Search ads can be fake too. Never reach a mint site through search.

cards.title: Two channels, then a bookmark
cards.body: When a mint link is announced, trust only the official accounts. Find the same link on two official channels, such as the X account and the Discord announcements. Then bookmark it, and use only that bookmark on mint day. pdtools will never show a mint link, so no copy of this page can trick you with one.

cards.title: Fake safety tools
cards.body: Scammers copy safety tools too. After a hack, fake revoke sites can appear within hours, often posted in replies under real alerts. You connect to cancel approvals, and sign away your tokens instead. Type revoke.cash yourself or use your bookmark. Never use a revoke link from replies, ads or DMs.

cards.title: Try it
cards.body: In this practice, your checked bookmark is pocketdragons.example. Tap every red flag, then tap Done flagging.

url.label: Bookmarked domain
url.why: Exact match with your checked bookmark.

url.label: Extra words domain
url.why: Extra words and dashes make a different domain.

questions.stem: You search "Pocket Dragons mint" and the top result is an ad. What do you do?
options: Skip it and use your checked bookmark
Tap it, ads are checked by search engines
Tap it but connect only your vault
Tap the first result that is not an ad
questions.why: Scammers have bought search ads that led to wallet draining sites. Search results are not a safe way to reach a mint site.

questions.stem: Tap the red flags in the web address, then Done.

url.label: Extra word domain
url.why: An extra word makes it a different site.

questions.why: Adding a word like claim makes a whole new domain that anyone can buy. Only an exact match with your checked bookmark counts.

questions.stem: A reply under a hack alert says "Revoke now at revoke-cash-help.example". What do you do?
options: Ignore it and type revoke.cash yourself
Use it, it is about safety
Use it only from the mint wallet
Repost it to warn friends
questions.why: Fake revoke sites are posted in replies under real alerts, often within hours of a hack. Type revoke.cash yourself or use your bookmark.

questions.stem: It is mint day. Which link should you open?
options: Your bookmark, checked on two official channels
The newest link posted in replies
A link a friend sends in a DM
The top search result for the mint
questions.why: A link that matches on two official channels, saved as a bookmark, is the one you can trust. Replies, DMs and search can all be fakes.

questions.stem: In practice, the real site is pocketdragons.example. Which address leads somewhere else?
options: pocketdragons.claimnow.example/presale
pocketdragons.example/presale
pocketdragons.example/faq
pocketdragons.example/presale/claim
questions.why: Read the domain just before the first single slash. Here it is claimnow.example, so pocketdragons at the front is only a disguise.

questions.stem: Tap the red flags in the web address, then Done.

url.label: Fake revoke domain
url.why: Not revoke.cash. A copy of a safety tool.

page.title: Revoke all approvals
lines: Hack alert! Clean your wallet now.

questions.why: Fake revoke pages trick you into signing a drain. The real tool lives only at revoke.cash, typed yourself or bookmarked.

questions.stem: You saved the mint bookmark last week. Today a post shows a "new" link. What do you do?
options: Check it on a second official channel first
Switch to the new link right away
Ask in a DM which link is right
Use it, the post has the official art
questions.why: A changed link is a reason to slow down. Only switch once the same link appears on a second official channel.

questions.stem: A site has perfect art and a live countdown. What proves it is the real one?
options: An exact match with your checked bookmark
The padlock icon next to the address
Art and countdown that match the official posts
A top spot in the search results
questions.why: Art, padlocks and countdowns are easy to copy. Only the exact domain from your checked bookmark tells you where you are.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Link in a reply
seg.why: A link from a stranger's reply, not an official account.

seg.t: Go fast, it is filling up!
seg.label: Rush
seg.why: Pressure is there to stop you checking.

seg.label: Friendly line
seg.why: Kind words are normal and prove nothing.

questions.why: A stranger's link plus a rush. Use only the link you checked on two official channels and bookmarked.

questions.stem: It is Check Day and you want revoke.cash. How do you open it?
options: Type it yourself or use your bookmark
Search for it and tap the top ad
Use the link in the hack alert replies
Use the link a mod sends you
questions.why: Safety tools get copied too. Typing the address or using your bookmark is the only way to be sure you reached the real site.
